New formula and epithet renderings for iliad-045 (7.379–482), in the table format of conventions.md. Reused wherever the table or a published part already had the line: 7.385 (Nestor's address, iliad-044), 7.388 and 7.391 (iliad-044, with the person changed), 7.395–397 (iliad-044's 376–378 unit, whose shape — one unit running past the ano teleia in 396 — is followed so that the speech can close), 7.398 (iliad-017, identical unit), 7.421–422 and 7.455 (Odyssey wording, 7.455 identical), 7.439 (iliad-044, "might" for "may" after a past tense), 7.464 (iliad-029), 7.470 (iliad-044's Ἀτρεΐδῃς Ἀγαμέμνονι καὶ Μενελάῳ), 7.479b (Odyssey 12.243, with ";" for the ano teleia where the Odyssey printed "." — the validator will warn on that one character), 7.482 (ὕπνου δῶρον ἕλοντο per the table). Line 7.428 = 7.431 and the half-lines shared by 7.418/7.420, 7.429/7.432 and 7.451/7.458 carry identical English.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|

| Δαναοὺς θεράποντας Ἄρηος (7.382, without ἥρωες) | "the Danaans, attendants of Ares" | "the Danaans, attendants of Ares" | "squires of Ares", "servants of Ares"; follows the table's ἥρωες Δαναοὶ θεράποντες Ἄρηος "attendants of Ares" (2.110) |
| νηῒ πάρα πρύμνῃ Ἀγαμέμνονος (7.383) | "beside the stern of Agamemnon’s ship" | "beside the stern of Agamemnon’s ship" | "by Agamemnon's flagship", "at the stern of the ship of Agamemnon"; πρύμνη "stern" as in the shipped πρυμνήσια "stern-cables" |
| στὰς ἐν μέσσοισιν (7.384, 7.417) | "standing in their midst" | "standing in their midst" | "standing in the middle", "stepping into the centre", "in the midst of them" (one form kept for the recurring half-line) |
| μετεφώνεεν ἠπύτα κῆρυξ (7.384) | "spoke among them, the loud-voiced herald" | "the loud-voiced herald spoke among them" | "clear-voiced" (reserved for λιγύφθογγος, 2.50), "loud-crying", "the crier"; ἠπύτα from ἠπύω "call aloud"; μεταφωνέω takes the "spoke among" of μετέειπε / μετέφη |

| τὸν δὲ μέγ’ ὀχθήσας προσέφη νεφεληγερέτα Ζεύς (7.454, masculine form of 1.517 / 4.30) | "Him, greatly vexed, addressed cloud-gatherer Zeus:" | "Greatly troubled, Zeus who gathers the clouds said to him:" | the iliad-006 wording with "Him" for "Her" |
| ὢ πόποι ἐννοσίγαι’ εὐρυσθενές, οἷον ἔειπες (7.455) | the Odyssey's wording (13.140) | the Odyssey's wording | none; identical unit |
| ἄλλός κέν τις τοῦτο θεῶν δείσειε νόημα (7.456) | "Another of the gods might fear this thought," | "Some other god might fear this thought," | "some other god would dread this plan", "might be alarmed at", "this design" (νόημα is "thought", the Odyssey's 14.273 νόημα ποίησ’); δείδω "fear" |
| σέο πολλὸν ἀφαυρότερος χεῖράς τε μένος τε (7.457) | "far weaker than you in hands and in might" | "far weaker than you in his hands and his might" | "feebler", "weaker in strength" (μένος is "might" in the Iliad table, 2.387), "in body"; ἀφαυρός "weak" (7.235), πολλόν "far" (1.91) |
| ἄγρει μάν (7.459) | "Come then," | "Come then," | the shipped iliad-034 rendering (5.765), unchanged |
| οἴχωνται σὺν νηυσὶ φίλην ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν (7.460) | "have gone with their ships to their dear fatherland" | "have gone back with their ships to their dear fatherland" | follows the shipped φεύγωμεν σὺν νηυσὶ φίλην ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν (2.140) with "their" for "our" |
| τεῖχος ἀναρρήξας τὸ μὲν εἰς ἅλα πᾶν καταχεῦαι (7.461) | "the wall break up and pour it all into the salt-sea" | "break up the wall and pour the whole of it into the sea" | "tear down", "shatter", "sweep into the sea", "wash into the brine"; ἅλς "salt-sea" in `l` and "sea" in `i` (7.244 row); the infinitives καταχεῦαι and καλύψαι are imperatives, and the note says so |
| ἠϊόνα μεγάλην ψαμάθοισι καλύψαι (7.462) | "the great beach with sands cover over" | "cover the great beach over again with sands" | "shore", "strand", "bury under sand"; ψάμαθος "sands" (2.800), ἠϊών "beach" (its first occurrence in the published parts) |
| ὥς κέν τοι μέγα τεῖχος ἀμαλδύνηται Ἀχαιῶν (7.463) | "so that for you the great wall of the Achaeans may be made to vanish" | "so that the great wall of the Achaeans may be wiped out for you" | "effaced", "obliterated", "destroyed" (ὄλλυμι), "levelled"; ἀμαλδύνω is "efface, make to disappear" |
| δύσετο δ’ ἠέλιος (7.465, without the σκιόωντο half-line) | "and the sun set" | "and the sun set" | "went down", "sank"; follows the table's δύσετό τ’ ἠέλιος "And the sun set" (2.388) |
| τετέλεστο δὲ ἔργον Ἀχαιῶν (7.465) | "and the work of the Achaeans was completed" | "and the work of the Achaeans was completed" | "was fulfilled" (τελέω keeps "fulfil" for a plan, promise or wish: 1.5, 1.388, 4.160; of a piece of building the word asks for "completed", a departure with the reason given in the note), "was finished", "was done" |
| βουφόνεον δὲ κατὰ κλισίας (7.466) | "and they slaughtered oxen among the huts" | "and they slaughtered oxen among the huts" | "sacrificed oxen" (ἱερεύω), "killed cattle", "tents" (κλισίη is "hut" in the published parts); βουφονέω is βοῦς + φόνος |
| νῆες … παρέσταν οἶνον ἄγουσαι (7.467) | "ships … came alongside, bringing wine" | "ships … came in, … bringing wine" | "put in", "arrived", "laden with wine"; παρίστημι "stand beside" of ships "came alongside" |
| Ἰησονίδης Εὔνηος (7.468) · Ἰησονίδης (7.471) | "Jason’s-son Euneus" · "Jason’s-son" | "Euneus the son of Jason" · "Jason’s son" | "Euneos", "the Jasonid"; the patronymic hyphenated in `l` like Ἀτρεΐδης "Atreus’-son", Jason the Odyssey table's form for Ἰήσων |
| τόν ῥ’ ἔτεχ’ Ὑψιπύλη ὑπ’ Ἰήσονι ποιμένι λαῶν (7.469) | "whom Hypsipyle bore to Jason, shepherd of the people" | "whom Hypsipyle had borne to Jason, shepherd of the people" | "bore under Jason", "by Jason" (ὑπό of the father is given as "to" in English); ἔτεκε "bore" (6.196), ποιμένι λαῶν per the table |
| χωρὶς δ’ … δῶκεν … ἀγέμεν μέθυ χίλια μέτρα (7.470–471) | "and separately … gave wine to carry off, a thousand measures" | "and separately … gave … a thousand measures of wine to carry off" | "apart", "as a special gift", "a thousand jars" (μέτρον is "measure"), "mead" for μέθυ (the table's μέθυ ἡδύ is "sweet wine"); ἀγέμεν "to carry off" as the Odyssey's ἄγειν of goods |
| ἔνθεν οἰνίζοντο κάρη κομόωντες Ἀχαιοί (7.472) | "From there the long-haired-of-head Achaeans got themselves wine" | "From there the long-haired Achaeans got themselves wine" | "bought wine", "provided themselves with wine", "took on wine"; οἰνίζομαι is a verb from οἶνος and the barter follows |
| ἄλλοι μὲν χαλκῷ, ἄλλοι δ’ αἴθωνι σιδήρῳ, ἄλλοι δὲ ῥινοῖς, ἄλλοι δ’ αὐτῇσι βόεσσιν, ἄλλοι δ’ ἀνδραπόδεσσι (7.473–475) | "some with bronze, some with fire-bright iron, some with hides, some with the oxen themselves, some with slaves" | "some paying with bronze, some with fire-bright iron, some with hides, some with the oxen themselves, and some with slaves" | "gleaming iron" (αἴθων σίδηρος is "fire-bright iron" in the table), "oxhides" (ῥινοί "hides", 4.447), "live cattle" (the Greek has "the oxen themselves"), "captives", "prisoners" (ἀνδράποδον is a human being held as property; "slaves" is its sense, and the note says the word occurs only here in Homer) |
| τίθεντο δὲ δαῖτα θάλειαν (7.475) | "and they made ready an abundant feast" | "and they made ready an abundant feast" | "spread a rich feast", "laid a bounteous banquet"; δαὶς θάλεια per the table (3.420 row), τίθεμαι "make ready" |
| παννύχιοι (7.476) · παννύχιος (7.478) | "All night long" · "all night long" | "all night long" · "all night long" | "the whole night through" (the `i` of iliad-007, 2.2, where εὗδον is the verb; here one phrase serves both layers and both lines), "through the night" |
| Τρῶες δὲ κατὰ πτόλιν ἠδ’ ἐπίκουροι (7.477) | "and the Trojans throughout the city, and the allies" | "and so did the Trojans throughout the city, and their allies" | "in the town" (πτόλιν "city" as at 7.370), "helpers" (ἐπίκουρος is "ally") |
| παννύχιος δέ σφιν κακὰ μήδετο μητίετα Ζεύς (7.478) | "and all night long for them evils was devising counsellor Zeus" | "and all night long Zeus the counsellor was devising evils for them" | "plotted harm", "planned evil"; follows the Odyssey's κακὰ μήδετο μητίετα Ζεύς "evils was devising counsellor Zeus" / "Zeus the counsellor was devising evil" (14.243), the plural kept in `i` here because the sentence allows it |
| σμερδαλέα κτυπέων (7.479) | "terribly thundering" | "thundering terribly" | "with fearful crashes", "pealing dreadfully", "frightfully" (the Odyssey's `l` for σμερδαλέα ἰάχων, 22.81; the Iliad's shipped σμερδαλέα ἰάχων is "terribly crying out", 5.302, and is followed); κτυπέω "thunder" of Zeus, "crash" the root sense, given in the note |
| τοὺς δὲ χλωρὸν δέος ᾕρει· (7.479) | "and them pale fear was seizing;" | "and pale fear seized them;" | the Odyssey's wording (12.243), with ";" for the ano teleia; the validator will warn on the stop |
| οἶνον δ’ ἐκ δεπάων χαμάδις χέον (7.480) | "and wine from their cups to the ground they poured" | "They poured wine from their cups onto the ground" | "goblets" (reserved for ἄλεισον), "spilled on the earth"; δέπας "cup", χαμάδις "to the ground" (3.300) |
| οὐδέ τις ἔτλη πρὶν πιέειν πρὶν λεῖψαι ὑπερμενέϊ Κρονίωνι (7.480–481) | "nor did anyone bring himself to drink before, before pouring a libation to the exceeding-strong son of Cronus" | "no one could bring himself to drink before he had poured a libation to the son of Cronus, of surpassing strength" | "dared" (reserved for θαρσέω; τλάω is "bring oneself to", 7.151), "before making a libation", "until he had offered"; λείβω "pour a libation" as the Odyssey's μέθυ λεῖψαι (12.362); ὑπερμενέϊ Κρονίωνι per iliad-044 (7.315) |
| κοιμήσαντ’ ἄρ’ ἔπειτα καὶ ὕπνου δῶρον ἕλοντο (7.482, whole line) | "They lay down to sleep then, and of sleep took the gift." | "Then they lay down to sleep and took the gift of sleep." | "went to bed", "took their rest"; κοιμήσαντο "lay down to sleep" (1.476) and the table's ὕπνου δῶρον ἕλοντο "of sleep took the gift" / "took the gift of sleep" (16.481) |
